guide.intro: Four steps. Your site's form posts to your own server, and your server forwards it here with the site's key.

create.title: Create the site here and copy the key
create.body: Use the form above. The key is shown once: save it the moment you see it. If you lose it, issue another key and revoke the old one once the site is sending with the new one.

env.title: Store the key in the site's environment
env.body: As VENDERCRM_API_KEY in the .env file or in the hosting environment variables. Never in the HTML, in browser JavaScript, or in the repository.

handler.title: Paste the handler on your server
handler.body: Pick your stack below and copy the code. The form points at your own endpoint, and that endpoint is what calls clientes.com.py.

verify.title: Test it with a real submission
verify.body: Fill in the form with your own number. Within seconds the contact appears and, if you set a target stage, so does the deal in the pipeline. If it doesn't, check your server log: the response says why.

security.serverSide: The key lives on the site's server. Put it in the browser and anyone can read it and write into your pipeline.
security.idempotency: Always send idempotency_key. With the same key, a retry or a double click doesn't create a duplicate contact.
security.phone: The phone number is required and is the contact's identity. We accept the Paraguayan local format (0981 123 456) and normalise it to +595.
security.spam: Add the honeypot and, if you can, Cloudflare Turnstile. Spam is stopped at your site, not inside the CRM.
security.nonBlocking: If clientes.com.py doesn't answer, still show the visitor the thank-you page and record the error in your log. Never lose a lead to a timeout.

platforms.label: Elementor
steps: Open the page with the form and start editing it in Elementor.
Select the form widget and go to «Actions After Submit».

platforms.label: Wix
steps: In the Wix dashboard go to «Automations» and create a new automation.
Choose «Form is submitted» as the trigger and select the site's form.
Choose «Send an HTTP request» (or «Webhook») as the action.
Method POST, paste the webhook URL and leave the body with the form's data.
Turn the automation on and send a test submission from the published site.

platforms.label: Zapier / Make
steps: Create a Zap (or a Make scenario) with the customer's form as the trigger.
Add the «Webhooks by Zapier» → «POST» step (in Make: HTTP module → «Make a request»).
Paste the webhook URL and choose JSON as the body format.
Map the form fields into the body as they come; no renaming needed, you pick which is which here afterwards.
Turn the Zap on and run a test.

platforms.label: Other / manual
steps: Any tool that can send a POST will do: Webflow Logic, Formidable, Contact Form 7 with a webhook plugin, or the site's own backend.
POST to the webhook URL with the form contents as JSON (we also accept form-data submissions).
No special header or separate key is needed: the URL is the credential.
Send a test submission and come back here to pick the fields.

diagnostics.title: Connection & troubleshooting
diagnostics.requiredNote: everything else is optional; don't send empty fields ("").

steps.idle1: Look at the site's server log. If it says 401: the key it sends isn't an active key for this site. Issue a new key below and update VENDERCRM_API_KEY on the hosting.
steps.idle2: If the log shows no attempt at all: the form isn't reaching its own handler. Check the <form>'s action and method, and that the handler is deployed.
steps.idle3: If the log shows a timeout or connection error: check the URL is exactly the one above, with https and no trailing slash.
steps.idle4: Run the curl test below with an active key. If it returns 201, the CRM is fine and the problem is on the site.
steps.ok1: Submissions are arriving. If one specific lead is missing, check the site's log for that submission: the response carries the reason.

fixes.invalid-key: The key the site sent doesn't match any active key. Issue a new key below, put it in VENDERCRM_API_KEY and try again.
fixes.revoked-key: The site is still sending a key you already revoked. Put the active key (or issue a new one below) in VENDERCRM_API_KEY and restart the site's app if needed.
fixes.site-inactive: The site is deactivated here, so every submission is rejected with 403. Activate it with the button above.
fixes.tenant-unavailable: Your account can't receive leads right now. Check the account status or contact us.
fixes.tenant-read-only: Your account is read-only (subscription expired or in grace). Once it's back in good standing, submissions flow again.
fixes.rate-limited: The site exceeded 60 submissions per minute. If it isn't spam, check the site isn't retrying in a loop.
fixes.turnstile-failed: The Turnstile token failed verification. Check the site sends turnstile_token and that the Cloudflare keys below belong to the same widget.
fixes.invalid-body: The data arrived but failed validation (422). Most common: empty email ("") instead of omitted, idempotency_key shorter than 8 characters, or malformed JSON. The site's log names the field.
fixes.phone-missing: The submission arrived without a phone, or the field has a different name (it must be phone, 6 to 30 characters). Check the input's name and the mapping in the handler.
fixes.unknown: The last submission failed for a reason we don't recognise. Run the curl test and read the full response.

diagnostics.noStageHint: Contacts are created but no deal: pick a target stage above and save.
diagnostics.testBody: Replace the key and run this. It tests the CRM without going through the site, so you know which side is broken. It creates a real test contact: delete it afterwards.

expect.201: 201 → the CRM works; if the site isn't sending, the problem is its handler or its key.
expect.401: 401 → the key is mistyped, revoked, or belongs to another site.
expect.422: 422 → a field in the body is invalid; the response says which.
expect.none: No response or connection error → the URL is wrong or the hosting blocks outbound HTTPS.

talleres.waPrefill: Hi, I run a workshop or technical service and I'd like more customers.

header.title: Be the one they call when something breaks
header.lead: When someone's car, air conditioner or wiring breaks down, they search Google and call the first one who shows up and answers. That call needs to be yours.
header.body: We work with auto shops, HVAC technicians, electricians, plumbers and home-service providers whose business depends on the phone ringing.

pains.eyebrow: What we see in workshops and services
pains.title: There's work out there. You just need to be found.
pains.body: Almost every technical-service customer arrives in a hurry: they search Google for "AC technician nearby" or "auto shop in Luque" and pick from the first results. Word of mouth is good, but it doesn't reach that person.
pains.bodyTwo: And when your hands are busy with a job, you can't answer WhatsApp. The customer doesn't wait — they call the next number.
symptoms: You rely on referrals and some weeks bring no new work

method.eyebrow: The method, applied to your workshop
method.title: From urgent call to booked job
method.lead: The same four steps as always, in the language of your workshop.

steps.title: Diagnosis
steps.body: We look at how people find you today, which services pay off best, and how many inquiries you lose by not replying in time.

steps.title: Attract
steps.body: Your Google Maps listing with reviews and coverage area, plus Google Ads for the urgent searches for your service.

steps.title: Convert
steps.body: Automatic WhatsApp replies while you're working, and follow-up on every quote you send until the customer decides.

steps.title: Measure and grow
steps.body: How many inquiries came in, how many turned into jobs, and what each customer cost. What works gets scaled up.

outcomes.title: What stays running in your business
outcomes.lead: A new flow of work that doesn't depend on someone recommending you that week.

items.name: Visible in emergencies
items.body: You show up when someone in your area searches for your service, backed by reviews that build trust.

items.name: No one goes unanswered
items.body: An automatic WhatsApp reply lets people know you'll get back to them soon, even with your hands full.

items.name: Quotes that close
items.body: Every quote sent gets followed up, instead of sitting forgotten in the chat.

items.name: Repeat maintenance customers
items.body: Service and maintenance reminders that bring back the customers you already have.

statement.text: When something breaks, whoever answers first wins.
statement.sub: Being that person isn't down to luck.

items.q: I work alone or with one helper. Does this still work for me?
items.a: Yes. It's exactly when you work alone that you lose the most inquiries. We adjust it to the volume you can actually handle.

items.q: Can you target only my area?
items.a: Yes. Ads and your Google listing are set up for the cities and neighborhoods where you work, so you don't pay for customers you can't serve.

items.q: How much do I need to spend on advertising?
items.a: It depends on the service and the area. In the diagnosis we give you a realistic range. Many technical services start with just Google Maps and reviews.

items.q: What about maintenance reminders?
items.a: We set up WhatsApp alerts for service, oil changes or AC cleaning, so the customer comes back to you instead of looking elsewhere.

meta.title: Privacy policy | clientes.com.py
meta.description: What data clientes.com.py collects, what it is used for, and your rights over it.

sections.title: What data we collect
sections.body: When you fill in the contact form we store what you send us: name, company, phone, email, industry and your message. The site also stores a first-party cookie that remembers which channel you arrived through (for example, an ad or a search), for a maximum of 90 days.

sections.title: What we use it for
sections.body: Only to answer your inquiry and arrange the conversation you requested. We don't send unsolicited mass emails, we don't sell or rent data to third parties, and we don't use your data for any purpose other than the one that motivated the contact.

sections.title: Where it is stored
sections.body: The data is stored on our own management platform, with access restricted to our team. The infrastructure providers we use to run the site process data only on our behalf.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can ask us at any time to see the data we hold about you, correct it or delete it. Write to us through any of the site's contact channels and we'll resolve it, in accordance with Paraguayan personal data protection law.

meta.title: Terms and conditions | clientes.com.py
meta.description: Conditions for using the clientes.com.py site and the information published on it.

sections.title: About this site
sections.body: clientes.com.py is the informational site of our business-growth service for Paraguayan companies. The content describes how we work; it does not constitute a contractual offer. The specific conditions of each service are agreed in writing with each client, after the diagnosis.

sections.title: No promised results
sections.body: We work with a method and with measurement, but no commercial result can be guaranteed in advance: it depends on the industry, the offer and the joint work. Distrust anyone who guarantees otherwise — we don't.

sections.title: Intellectual property
sections.body: The content of this site — texts, brand and design — is ours. You may quote it citing the source; copying it for commercial use without authorization is not allowed.

sections.title: Governing law
sections.body: This site is governed by the laws of the Republic of Paraguay. Any dispute is submitted to the ordinary courts of the city of Asunción.

footer.tagline: We win customers and sales for Paraguayan SMBs: advertising, WhatsApp and follow-up, all measured.
